newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end up, Dec sets new high.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end up, Dec sets new high.

text.p: December CME live cattle futures shruged off early profit taking and ran up to post a new contact high by the close. Other months followed but gains were limited by continued expectations of increased fed cattle supplies going into next year, traders said.
December live cattle ran up to post a new contract high of 68.975 cents per lb before closing 0.325 higher at 68.900 cents. Other months finished 0.225 higher to 0.125 lower.
Early profit taking gave way to continued support prompted by the strong tone to cash markets and tight supply of choice cattle. Fund short covering added to strength, traders said.
"As long we continue this kind of cash price, I think its going to hold up the December (futures)," said Karl Skold, Director of Research for Frontier Risk Management.
Cash cattle traded at $72 to $74 per cwt earlier in the week and December futures started this week with a big discount at 66.725 cents, traders said.
The noon CST lightweight choice boxed beef value was quoted slightly lower at $118.21 per cwt, but remained at its highest price level since August 1993.
Deferred contracts, although showing some short covering interest, remained pressured from larger supply projections.

Early indications on next Friday's cattle on feed report generally pointed to continued heavy placements onto feedlots during October and on-feed supplies rising to near year ago levels, analysts said.

Merrill Lynch, R.J. O'Brien and Cargill Investor Services bought December late. Prudential Securities and Refco sold February at the close while RBH bought February and sold December, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commission houses bought December calls late with volatility up. Commercials sold February 66 calls, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures were influenced by action in corn and live cattle pits. Prices fell late before recovering at the close when corn futures fell and live cattle moved ujp to new highs, traders said.
Early support reflected the rising CME feeder cattle index. The latest index was up $0.41 to $64.43 per cwt, a two week gain of $2.45 and highest level since December 27, 1995.

Smith Barney, ADM Investor Services and E.D.&F. Man bought early while Cargill Investor Services spread long May feeders/short October live cattle. Refco notably sold November on its setback, pit sources said.
Feeder cattle closed 0.650 cent lower to 0.175 higher with November off most. January ended 0.175 lower at 67.400 cents.
